content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review.

- [Specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all checks passed; no unresolved clarifications

The proposed MVP covers saving, editing, searching, tagging, filtering, favoriting, archiving, restoring, and deleting bookmarks. It assumes a personal single-user app; accounts, sharing, imports, extensions, and automatic page metadata are deferred.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll create the implementation plan.

This looks like a solid starting point. It covers what I mainly need — saving links, giving them titles and notes, finding them again with search, tags, and filters, and keeping things tidy with editing, archiving, restoring, and deleting. That's the heart of what I asked for.

One thing I want to make sure I understand: since you're deferring automatic page info, that means when I save a link I'll always have to type the title myself, right? I can live with that for a first version, but I'd want to revisit having the app fill in the title for me down the road.

Otherwise this matches what I had in mind. Approved — please go ahead and create the implementation plan.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review. No application code or task breakdown has been created yet.

Key decisions:

- React 19 and TypeScript client built with Vite, following the supported React/Vite setup. [React guidance](https://react.dev/learn/build-a-react-app-from-scratch)
- Express 5 API and production server.
- SQLite persistence through `better-sqlite3`, with migrations, transactions, foreign keys, and WAL mode. [`better-sqlite3` documentation](https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3)
- One production process on `0.0.0.0:4000`.
- User-entered titles remain required; automatic page information is still deferred.
- Unit, integration, component, accessibility, responsive, and end-to-end testing are planned.

Artifacts:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- [HTTP API contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [UI behavior contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/ui-behavior.md)
- [Validation quickstart](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)

Branch identifier: `001-bookmark-manager`

The API contract passes structural validation. Its sole lint warning is that the input-free health endpoint has no `4XX` response, which is intentional.

Please approve the plan or request changes. After approval, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered implementation tasks.

The plan sounds thorough, and the way you've described how the app will behave matches what I want — adding links, opening them, searching, tagging, filtering, favoriting, sorting, and the archive-then-delete flow with a confirmation so I don't lose things by accident. I like that deleting something takes a deliberate step.

The technical choices are over my head, but I trust your judgment there as long as the app ends up doing what we've described. I see titles are still typed by hand and automatic page info is deferred — that's fine for this version, as we agreed.

Approved — go ahead and generate the implementation tasks.

content:
The bookmark manager is built and ready for review at:

**http://maker:4000/**

Implemented:

- Save links with manually entered titles, notes, and tags
- Search, tag filtering, favorites, and four sort modes
- Editing, archiving, restoring, and confirmed permanent deletion
- Duplicate-address warnings
- Durable SQLite storage across restarts
- Responsive desktop/mobile layouts and accessible keyboard behavior

Validation passed:

- 59/59 implementation tasks complete
- 31 unit, integration, API, persistence, and component tests
- 12 end-to-end tests across desktop and mobile
- Automated WCAG A/AA scan
- 1,000-bookmark performance checks
- Clean production build and health/readiness smoke test
- 0 dependency vulnerabilities reported

Details are recorded in [validation.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/validation.md) and [README.md](/work/README.md). No login is required.

I took the app for a spin, and it does exactly what I set out to build. I saved a link with a title, notes, and tags, found it again by searching (even with different capitalization), filtered by tag, marked it a favorite, and got a clear warning when I tried to save the same address twice. Archiving pulled it out of my main list but kept it safe in the archive, restoring brought it back intact, and permanently deleting it took a deliberate step. The starting screen is welcoming and clear about how to begin.

That's the whole heart of what I wanted — a place to save links and keep them organized and tidy. I'm happy with this. As we agreed, typing titles by hand and having the app fill them in automatically is something to look at in a future version, but it doesn't hold anything back here.

Accepted — thank you, this is what I was hoping for.
